chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Sallam al-Muta'abbid, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to Sudeyr:
O Sudeyr! Whoever swears by Allah falsely has disbelieved, and whoever swears by Allah truthfully has sinned.
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And do not make Allah an obstacle for your swearing of oaths' [2:224].

key_terms.أَثِمَ: Sinned/committed ithm — a serious sin, though less grave than kufr
key_terms.حَلَفَ بِاللَّهِ: To swear by Allah — invoking God's name as a witness to one's oath
key_terms.عُرْضَةً: An obstacle, target, or subject of frequent exposure — here meaning making Allah's name routine/habitual in oaths
key_terms.كَفَرَ: Disbelieved/committed kufr — the gravest category of transgression

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about swearing oaths by Allah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses his companion Sudeyr al-Sairafi in a private teaching, delivering a stern ruling about oaths: even truthful oaths are sinful because they reduce the sacred Name of God to a rhetorical device. The Imam supports this with Quran 2:224, which originally addressed those who used oaths by Allah as an excuse to avoid righteous deeds. The original audience would have understood this as establishing a hierarchy: lying oaths constitute kufr (disbelief) — a graver category — while even sincere oaths constitute ithm (sin) due to the casual use of God's sacred name.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Abu Sallam Al Mutabbad that, ‘He heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying to Sudeyr: ‘O Sudeyr!
The one who swears by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a liar has disbelieved, and the one who swears by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a truthful has sinned,
[2:224] And make not Allah an excuse for your swearing’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Yahya ibn Ibrahim from his father from abu Salam al-Salam al-Muta‘abbid who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying to Sadir, ‘O Sadir,
one who swears by Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, falsely as well as one who swears by Allah truthfully has sinned;
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘Do not swear by Allah, unless you are obligated.’ [2:224]”
